jobs.title: Regional Sales Director, Enterprise - EMEA
jobs.description_text:
About the Job:

As a Regional Sales Director, you’ll own Enterprise sales performance and strategy within EMEA. You’ll lead a high-performing team of experienced Enterprise Account Executives focused on new business and expansion opportunities, building the pipeline, sales discipline, and customer relationships needed to deliver predictable growth.

You’ll collaborate cross-functionally to drive regional performance and support complex enterprise sales engagements. This role is ideal for a sales leader who understands the developer tools space, is passionate about solving complex customer challenges, and thrives in a high-growth SaaS environment. This role reports to our VP, EMEA.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead, develop, and manage a team of Enterprise Account Executives across EMEA, driving new logo acquisition and expansion within existing enterprise accounts.
  • Own quarterly and annual team revenue targets, translating regional strategy into clear territory plans and execution priorities.
  • Build a strong outbound pipeline generation culture, partnering with Sales Development and Marketing to create and progress qualified opportunities.
  • Own regional sales forecasting and pipeline inspection, ensuring accurate reporting, clear deal qualification, and proactive management of risks and gaps.
  • Coach Account Executives through complex sales cycles, including discovery, value articulation, stakeholder engagement, negotiation, and close planning.
  • Provide executive sponsorship for strategic opportunities and customer relationships, helping the team engage senior technical and business decision-makers.
  • Partner with senior leadership and Revenue Operations on annual planning, territory assignments, coverage, capacity, and quota and compensation planning.
  • Work closely with Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Marketing, Sales Development, Revenue Operations, and Enablement to improve sales execution and deliver a coordinated customer experience.
  • Recruit, onboard, develop, and retain high-performing sales talent, fostering an inclusive culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

  • Lead, develop, and manage a team of Enterprise Account Executives across EMEA, driving new logo acquisition and expansion within existing enterprise accounts.
  • Own quarterly and annual team revenue targets, translating regional strategy into clear territory plans and execution priorities.

jobs.title: Corporate Regional Sales Director - EMEA
jobs.description_text:
About the Job:

LaunchDarkly is looking for a  Corporate Regional Sales Director EMEA to lead the strategy and execution of our Corporate EMEA sales business. This leader will own regional performance across new business and expansion, lead and develop frontline sales leadership and Account Executives, and build the operating discipline needed for predictable growth.

The role combines hands-on commercial leadership with organizational leadership. The Regional Sales Director will set the regional plan, inspect pipeline and forecast, coach leaders through complex deals, shape territory and capacity decisions, and partner closely with Marketing, SDR, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, and Enablement.

This role is designed for a sales leader who can operate across Corporate EMEA segments, translate global strategy into regional execution, and build a high-performing, accountable, and inclusive team in a fast-growing SaaS environment.

Responsibilities:

  • Own Corporate EMEA performance and strategy. Set the regional plan for new logo acquisition, expansion, pipeline creation, coverage, and revenue attainment across the Corporate EMEA business.
  • Lead through frontline managers. Develop and support sales managers and Account Executives through clear goals, consistent operating rhythms, coaching, and performance management.
  • Drive predictable forecasting. Own forecast accuracy, pipeline inspection, stage discipline, deal progression, and risk management across the region; provide clear updates and actions to senior leadership.
  • Build pipeline and improve conversion. Establish expectations for prospecting, partner with SDR and Marketing leaders on pipeline generation, and remove barriers to conversion across the funnel.
  • Coach complex sales execution. Support strategic opportunities, executive alignment, multi-threading, value articulation, negotiation, and close plans across technical and business stakeholders.
  • Shape territory, coverage, and capacity. Partner with Revenue Operations and senior sales leadership on territory design, segmentation, headcount planning, quota allocation, hiring priorities, and organizational structure.
  • Build the team. Recruit, onboard, retain, and develop high-performing sales talent; create a strong management bench and an inclusive culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations. 

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

  • Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages
  • Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts
  • Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize
  • Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types
  • Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights

jobs.title: Manager, Corporate Sales - London
jobs.description_text:
About the Job:

LaunchDarkly helps developers de-risk every release and deliver better software faster. As Manager, Corporate Sales — EMEA, you’ll lead and develop a team of Corporate Account Executives focused on new business and expansion opportunities across the region.

You’ll own the team’s revenue targets and provide hands-on coaching across pipeline generation, discovery, deal progression, forecasting, and customer engagement. You’ll build a consistent operating rhythm, help Account Executives develop their skills, and partner cross-functionally to turn regional priorities into strong execution.

This role is ideal for a sales leader who enjoys developing talent, stays close to the details of the business, and brings a disciplined, customer-focused approach to selling technical solutions.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Corporate Account Executives to achieve quarterly and annual revenue targets across new business and expansion.
  • Establish a consistent outbound prospecting and pipeline generation rhythm, partnering with Marketing and Sales Development to create and convert qualified opportunities.
  • Provide hands-on coaching through call reviews, one-on-ones, pipeline reviews, and deal strategy sessions to strengthen discovery, qualification, value articulation, negotiation, and close execution.
  • Own the team’s sales forecast, inspect pipeline quality and deal progression, and identify risks and actions early to improve predictability.
  • Set clear performance expectations, monitor individual and team results, and use data to identify coaching priorities and support improvement.
  • Partner with Account Executives on key customer relationships and complex opportunities, helping them engage technical and business stakeholders and build compelling business cases.
  • Hire, onboard, develop, and retain high-performing sales talent; build an inclusive culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
  • Collaborate with Solutions Engineering, Marketing, Sales Development, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, and Enablement to improve sales execution and support a coordinated customer experience.
  • Maintain strong Salesforce and sales-tool discipline, ensuring accurate opportunity data, clear next steps, and reliable performance reporting.
  • Contribute field insights and practical recommendations to Corporate Sales strategy, sales methodologies, process improvements, and regional initiatives.

Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated success in SaaS sales, including a strong track record in a quota-carrying closing role and 3+ years of sales management or team leadership experience.
  • Proven ability to lead teams to meet or exceed revenue targets in a Corporate, Commercial, SMB, or Mid-Market sales environment.
  • Experience building outbound pipeline and coaching Account Executives across the full sales cycle.
  • Strong forecasting, pipeline management, and analytical skills, with the ability to translate performance data into clear actions.
  • Experience hiring, onboarding, coaching, and developing sales talent, including addressing performance gaps constructively.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and negotiation skills, with the ability to build credibility with customers and cross-functional partners.
  • Experience selling to technology buyers or developer-centric audiences; familiarity with the software development lifecycle, DevOps, or feature management tools is a plus.
  • Familiarity with MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, or comparable sales methodologies, and the ability to reinforce them through practical coaching.
  • Ability to operate with urgency, adaptability, and sound judgment in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • A collaborative leadership style and genuine commitment to mentoring

You'll own Legora's partnerships with top law schools across Europe, working closely with faculty, school administration, and Legora's own sales and engagement teams, to get the next generation of lawyers trained on and excited about Legora.
We're building this program from the ground up in Europe — there's no inherited playbook here. You'll be one of the founding members of Legora's partnerships team on the ground, shaping how we bring Legora into legal curricula and how we build lasting relationships with the schools that matter most. You'll work alongside Legora's broader partnerships team in New York, and closely with Sales, Engagement Management, and Legal Engineers in Europe.
What You'll Do
Build and manage relationships with top law schools across Europe, getting students access to Legora through complimentary licenses.
Go beyond access — make sure students are genuinely learning on Legora, so they graduate as trained users and evangelists for the platform.
Team up with professors to embed Legora into the curriculum, identifying the faculty who are the real movers and shakers and figuring out what will get them excited about building a partnership around Legora.
Get embedded with Legora's sales and customer teams so you understand the product well enough to demo it and speak to it credibly with schools.
Track engagement and outcomes across your school partnerships, and report on progress.
Bring feedback from schools and faculty back into Legora to inform product and go-to-market decisions.

A law school background, ideally including experience at a large law firm, and some time spent actually practicing law.
Legal education and practice experience in Europe: you've studied and practiced law in the region and understand how European law schools and legal careers work.
A genuine interest in doing partnerships rather than continuing to practice law.
Comfort building a partner program rather than inheriting one. Meaning you're fine when the structure doesn't exist yet.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills as you'll be working with professors, school administrators, and students, as well as Legora's internal teams.
Ability to run multiple relationships and priorities at once, across several schools simultaneously.
Comfort with a product that ships fast — you'll stay current and help the schools you work with do the same.
Willingness to travel to visit schools and build relationships across Europe.
Nice to have:
Familiarity with AI products and how to talk about them to an audience that's still building trust in AI — being a curious, regular user of AI tools count

jobs.title: GTM Engineer
jobs.description_text:
Multiverse is the upskilling platform for AI and Tech adoption.
We have partnered with 1,500+ companies to deliver a new kind of learning that's transforming today’s workforce.
Our upskilling apprenticeships are designed for people of any age and career stage to build critical AI, data, and tech skills. Our learners have driven $2bn+ ROI for their employers, using the skills they’ve learned to improve productivity and measurable performance.
In April 2026, we announced $70 million in strategic funding, led by Schroders Capital, with participation from StepStone Group, Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst. At an increased valuation of $2.1bn, the round makes us Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn.
But we aren’t stopping there. With a strong operational footprint and 800+ employees, we have ambitious plans to continue scaling. We’re building a world where tech skills unlock people’s potential and output.
Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.
What You’ll Do
Build AI workflow automation. Design, build and ship AI-powered workflows that remove manual GTM work; from lead research and CRM enrichment to call analysis, personalised outreach and lifecycle automation. Own builds end to end, from problem definition through deployment, monitoring and iteration.
Bridge gaps between systems. Find creative ways to connect tools that do not natively integrate. Build the webhooks, middleware, scripts and glue that keep data flowing cleanly between Salesforce and the rest of the stack.
Solve multi-departmental integration challenges. Work across the boundaries of Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Data and Finance to turn tangled, cross-functional processes into reliable, automated systems.
Prototype, test and scale. Test new ideas at small scale, measure what works, and scale the versions that deliver. Bring a bias to ship a working prototype over a perfect specification.
Build with AI as the default. Use LLMs, agentic workflows, MCP builds and evals as everyday tools. Ask “how would AI do this?” before reaching for headcount or manual effort.
Own reliability. Treat what you build as production systems: instrument them, monitor them, handle failure gracefully, and reduce risk across the GTM tech stack.
Evaluate and recommend. Run structured pilots of new tools, assess capability, integration fit, reliability and ROI, and make clear build-versus-buy recommendations.
Set the standard. Document what you build, enable GTM teams to adopt it with confidence, and mentor others in the team on building with AI and automation.
What You’ll Bring
Significant hands-on experience in RevOps, GTM Systems, or Sales Operations within enterprise technology, ideally in a structured qualification environment such as MEDDPICC. You understand the full GTM engine and you know what good looks like when real revenue depends on the systems you own.
Solid data and systems fundamentals. You understand CRM data models, object relationships, data quality and reporting architecture, and you design builds that keep data clean and trustworthy at scale.
A track record of building for internal GTM teams. Your strongest work is systems and workflows used every day by sales, marketing or CS teams inside a business, not only side projects, single-client builds or customer-facing pre-sales work.
A builder’s mindset on top of that foundation. You have built things, not just configured them. You can point to workflows, automations, integrations or tools you shipped that moved a real metric, ideally things nobody explicitly asked you to build.
You learn systems fast. You pick up unfamiliar platforms quickly and reason about how they fit together. You are comfortable reading API documentation, handling authentication, respecting rate limits, and parsing JSON when a native connector does not exist.

jobs.title: Principal Engineer, Data Quality Platform
jobs.description_text:
Institutional Fabric for the Digital Asset Market
Founded in 2018, Talos provides institutional-grade trading technology for the global digital asset market, powering many of the major players in the crypto ecosystem. Our mission is clear: to advance the mass adoption of digital assets by seamlessly connecting institutions to the digital asset ecosystem. We are committed to building the most innovative and trusted platform in the world, supporting the entire trading lifecycle.
At Talos, you’ll find an environment that champions kindness and respect, values diverse perspectives, and upholds inclusivity at every turn. We believe every member of our team brings invaluable insights and abilities that drive Talos forward. In our pursuit of excellence, we foster a culture of trust, integrity, collaboration, and mutual growth.
We are a tight-knit yet globally distributed team of highly experienced engineers and business leaders, with hubs in New York, London, Singapore, and Cyprus. You’ll be part of a hybrid-friendly environment where your unique talents and insights will play a crucial role in building something extraordinary.
 Principal Engineer, Data Quality Platform
You'll own data correctness across Talos. You'll lead the data quality engineering team, run BAU data operations, and own reference and security master data, along with the pipelines and platform that deliver it.
Our goal: the data we return to clients is always correct, and we find defects before a client does.
You'll join a small team with the mandate to work independently from product engineering and challenge it. Engineering teams make assumptions about how their systems behave. Your job is to test those assumptions and prove or disprove them with evidence.
 
Responsibilities
Lead AI-first data quality engineering
Validate every client-facing endpoint continuously. The focus is our REST and WebSocket APIs. Cloud delivery (S3, Snowflake, Databricks) is also in scope. Assert correctness against independent sources of truth, across every environment and client entitlement.
Cover streaming as well as request/response. For WebSocket, that means:
sequencing and gap detection
snapshot-to-increment consistency
reconnect and replay correctness
staleness of live subscriptions
agreement between the streamed view and the REST view of the same state
Use adaptive detection, not static thresholds. Learn baselines per endpoint and per market, and let them adjust as "normal" changes. Hand-set limits get noisy, go stale, and teach people to ignore alerts.
Apply LLM and agentic tooling to generate checks from API specs and schemas, keep them current as the product changes, and triage alerts before a human sees them. Know when a deterministic rule, invariant or cross-source reconciliation is the better tool.
Test resilience and load. Design load, performance and failure-mode tests.
When you find a fault, raise it with the owning team with enough evidence for them to act. Drive it to resolution, then add a check that would have caught it earlier.
Measure and publish endpoint and field coverage, time to detect, detected-before-client rate and false-positive rate.
Run data governance
Build and maintain a catalog of our data assets and APIs, covering lineage and downstream consumers. Maintain an understanding of assets, how they're used and what breaks when they change.
Own data governance tooling such as OpenMetadata.
Own reference and security master data
Lead the build-out of the next-generation security master platform, then run it day to day: new listings, symbol mapping across venues, and increment and contract specs.
Design processes for safe updates to security entries, with validation and rollback.
Expand coverage across the firm
Over time, extend data quality coverage beyond client APIs to:
trade signals
pre-trade analytics
client post-trade analysis
PMS analytics
Qualifications
A track record of leading data QA or data quality teams, preferably on market data or other high-thr
